A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RapTB/SubM research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original SMILES, Expr24, and CommonGen experiments, including benchmark results, ablations, and prefix-collapse diagnostics in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, antimicrobial-peptide generation, model-scaling experiments, and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The RapTB objective, absorbed backups, termination stop-gradients, and SubM selection procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the objective/implementation details match between v1 Appendices C–D and v2 Appendices F–G. Additional comparators and tested backbones do not revise the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds antimicrobial-peptide generation with an amino-acid vocabulary and biological reward structure (Appendix B.3, Table 22), substantially extending task and domain coverage. SMILES, its longer-horizon test, Expr24, and the CommonGen diagnostic subset are retained.

E2.justification: PPO and GRPO are added to both the SMILES and Expr24 comparisons (Tables 1 and 3). V2 also reports an AvgPrefixTB comparison in Table 21 and includes DynaPPO, COMs, and a standard GFlowNet comparator in the AMP comparison (Table 22). Existing comparators, including RootSubTBLogZ, remain.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 3B/8B Llama and 32B Qwen3 configurations, controlled hyperparameter sweeps, and AMP performance/diversity/novelty evaluation with reported budgets of 3K, 5K, or 10K steps (Appendices B–D). These are added experimental settings; the original sampling protocols and default hyperparameter tables are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds beta/rho sensitivity grids on SMILES and Expr24, plus auxiliary-weight and minimum-prefix-depth ablations on Expr24 (Tables 24–27). The AvgPrefixTB comparison tests whether dense prefix supervision alone suffices, while the scaling study probes whether collapse persists with greater model capacity. Existing ablations and prefix/length diagnostics remain.

E5.justification: The six-run SMILES summary, three-seed Expr24 results, reported 95% confidence intervals, and t-based aggregation procedure are unchanged. The added experiments provide no new explicit run-count disclosures, uncertainty-estimation methods, or significance tests; their additional point estimates do not establish changed statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Original results are retained, including RapTB+SubM's SMILES Score 0.844 and Expr24 NormCov 0.209. New entries include AvgPrefixTB's SMILES entropy 0.665, AMP RapTB+SubM performance 0.916 at 3K steps, and its 32B SMILES Score 0.867/FPDiv 0.896 (Tables 21–23), alongside RL and sensitivity results. These are newly reported comparisons and settings, not improvements over matched v1 runs.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 adds a fixed-point argument distinguishing unabsorbed and absorbed objectives, including a conditional bound on TB loss at a global RapTB minimizer using a zero-TB solution with finite auxiliary cost. Appendix B.2 formally defines AvgPrefixTB. The existing appendix derivations otherwise remain unchanged after renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and central RapTB/SubM contributions remain unchanged. The introduction and conclusion extend the stated validation claims to RL/alternative GFlowNet comparisons, biological sequences, two architecture families, and model scales up to 32B.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly qualifies preservation of the TB optimum under reward absorption, explains AvgPrefixTB's short-sequence behavior and hyperparameter trade-offs, and discusses length-inflated AMP diversity. It also interprets scaling results as evidence of structural, architecture-independent behavior. These substantially expand the original mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: V2 documents shared backbone, LoRA rank, and reward information for the RL comparisons; rank and reward/decoding consistency for scaling; and AMP step budgets. The detailed original LoRA, grammar, scheduling, and replay specifications are retained in Appendix G. No new code or data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds targeted positioning relative to entropy-regularized RL, describes TBA's systems contributions as complementary, and adds GRPO and molecular-representation/diffusion references. The original positioning around TB-family objectives and replay coverage remains intact.

P1.justification: There are targeted introduction, results, and conclusion revisions, plus new Appendices B–D that shift the original metrics, derivations, and implementation appendices to E–G. Most existing prose and the main section order remain unchanged. The first-page preprint notice also changes to conference proceedings text.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands tabular presentation: Tables 1 and 3 gain RL rows, and Tables 21–27 add baseline, AMP, scaling, and sensitivity displays. Existing Figures 1–5 are retained, while several tables, plots, and Algorithm 1 move with the revised layout; later appendix tables are renumbered rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: Section 3.4 clarifies absorption's effect on exact balance, and Appendices B–D address previously untested questions about simple prefix supervision, model scale, and tuning sensitivity. These improve interpretability and empirical support. However, missing uncertainty estimates and sparse setup details limit the new studies, AMP comparisons use unequal budgets, and architecture-independence claims exceed what testing two families establishes. The net quality gain is supported but limited.
